sections.title: Core Foundations & Conceptual Framework
sections.content:
• **Accession**: Aziz-ud-din (Alamgir II) was the son of Jahandar Shah, brought from prison to the throne by **Imad-ul-Mulk** (Wazir) in 1754.
• **Political Reality**: The Emperor was a mere figurehead; real power rested with the Wazir, who controlled the treasury and administration.
• **External Threat**: The reign was defined by the repeated invasions of **Ahmad Shah Abdali**, who captured Delhi in 1757.
• **Key Metric / Factor**: The total collapse of the 'Mansabdari' system and the inability of the center to pay the army led to the rise of independent regional states.

items.definition: The powerful Wazir who blinded Ahmad Shah (predecessor) and installed Alamgir II; he was the primary architect of the empire's administrative paralysis.
Abdali sacked Delhi and Mathura; he appointed Najib-ud-Daulah as 'Mir Bakshi' to keep a check on the Wazir, further weakening the Emperor.

items.title: Major Applications / Initiatives
items.content:
• **Administrative Decay**: The 'Jagirdari' crisis reached its peak; land grants were given to non-existent or non-performing officials.
• **Diplomatic Failure**: Inability to form a coalition against Afghan invaders due to internal court factionalism.

items.title: Challenges & Way Forward
items.content:
• **Key Challenges**: Constant threat of assassination; the Emperor was eventually murdered by his own Wazir in 1759.
• **Solutions**: Historical analysis focuses on the failure of the 'Centralized Autocracy' model in the 18th century.

items.title: Mnemonic for Retention
items.content:
• **Memory Acronym**: 'A-I-A' (Alamgir, Imad, Abdali).
• **Decoded Meaning**: Alamgir II was controlled by Imad (Wazir) and terrorized by Abdali (Invader).

upscNotes.content: Examiner Trap: UPSC often confuses the 'Battle of Plassey' (1757) with the 'Abdali Invasion' (1757). Remember: Plassey was in Bengal (British rise), while Abdali's invasion was in Delhi (Mughal collapse).
Mains Value Addition: Use the term 'Political Vacuum' to describe the period between 1754-1759, where the Mughal Emperor was a 'prisoner of his own court'.

keyTakeaways: Alamgir II was a puppet ruler under Wazir Imad-ul-Mulk.
His reign saw the peak of Afghan influence under Ahmad Shah Abdali.
The assassination of Alamgir II in 1759 signaled the total loss of imperial dignity.
